§10.5.4 Tables Inside Forms

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

forms-tables-inside-forms · forms tables

✅ Normative

Inside a form, a table MUST be used only for a genuine grid: one shared set of printed column headers over repeating rows of the same shape, or a printed row-by-column matrix. Where it is ambiguous, the fields SHOULD be rendered as individual field lines.

Numbered form lines are never table rows

A line with its own caption and one amount box is a field line, even when the amount boxes align into a ruled column. It MUST be rendered as a field line, not as a table row: the alignment is typesetting, the caption is the structure.

Dollars and cents printed in two ruled columns MUST be rendered as one value — 1,234.00 — never split.

A matrix keeps its blank corner

The empty corner header of a matrix MUST be kept. Dropping it shifts every heading one column left:

<table>
  <tr><th></th><th>Beginning</th><th>Ending</th></tr>
  <tr><td>Profit</td><td>1.0000000000 %</td><td>1.0000000000 %</td></tr>
  <tr><td>Loss</td><td>1.0000000000 %</td><td>1.0000000000 %</td></tr>
  <tr><td>Capital</td><td>1.0000000000 %</td><td>1.0000000000 %</td></tr>
</table>

This is the rule of a blank corner cell in any table§9.3.1.

Cells carry the normal form notation

  • A checkbox cell MUST be rendered [x] or [ ]. A blank cell intended to be checked is a checkbox; a blank cell not intended to be checked stays empty.
  • Every printed row MUST be emitted, blank rows included, as full rows of empty cells. Rows MUST NOT be merged, reordered or added.
  • Each entry belongs to its own row's rule lines, never to a neighbour's. Insurance-application coverage grids are the stress test.
  • A cell containing form fields MUST use the normal form notation, as list items inside the cell.
<tr><td>Jane</td><td>Doe</td><td>987-65-4321</td><td>Daughter</td><td>[x]</td><td>[ ]</td></tr>
<tr><td></td><td></td><td></td><td></td><td>- [ ]</td><td>- [ ]</td></tr>

A table as a field's value

Some keyed entries take a grid as their value. The key MUST stay a normal field line, and the table MUST be placed below it, indented to the list item's content column, with a blank line on each side:

- \[J\] **Partner's share of profit, loss, and capital (see instructions):**

  <table>
    <tr><th></th><th>Beginning</th><th>Ending</th></tr>
    <tr><td>Profit</td><td>1.0000000000 %</td><td>1.0000000000 %</td></tr>
  </table>

- **Check if decrease is due to sale or exchange of partnership interest.**: [ ]

The indent is load-bearing. An indented table belongs to the list item, so the list — and the depth of everything after it — survives. A flush-left table between bullets ends the list and flattens everything that follows.

Not every table on a form page is form content

A large standalone data table that is not part of the fillable form — an embedded financial schedule — is an ordinary table. See Is This Even a Table§9.1.5.

✅ Sample — a self-certification form built from grids

Part III prints two side-by-side asset grids sharing one header row (Type of Asset, (A) Cash Value*, (B) Annual Income), each rendered as its own table; Parts I, II and IV are field lines, and the description tables under Parts III and IV are empty pre-printed rows. Several empty value cells print only a $ — see Fill-Ins§10.4.4.
